subject: Weekly Exec Staff Snapshot: Traction, Chokepoints & QBR asks
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Exec Staff <exec-staff@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Park <susan@acme-data.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@cloudforge.io>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly Exec Staff Snapshot: Traction, Chokepoints & QBR asks

Hi all —

Quick snapshot ahead of Friday's QBR dry run. TL;DR: commercial traction is trending above plan but we have two capacity-related chokepoints that need decisions this week. Attachments: QBR-deck-v2 (high level slides) and prefix_metrics.csv (per-customer token mix).

Wins
- Acme Data: proof-of-value completed; pilot expanded to +3 internal teams. Early latency KPIs are within SLA for 95th pct for 8k contexts.
- Hosted API revenue: MRR growth +18% MoM for the sales-sourced accounts in Q2 cohort.
- Optimize recommendations: initial quantization profile reduced per-token cost ~17% on testbench.

Risks / Chokepoints
1) Dedicated capacity fill / GPU mismatch: customer spike last week saturated the p4d pool; autoscale policy didn’t kick in because burst budget was exhausted. We need to approve either (A) a short-term burst credit for Dedicated (90 days) or (B) re-route non-critical traffic to a cheaper model variant during peak. Impact: potential 2–3% revenue at risk this quarter if not mitigated.
2) QBR data hygiene: prefix_metrics.csv shows several enterprise tenants sending mixed short/long prompt patterns causing suboptimal batching. This impacts cost estimates for a subset of accounts (notably Acme).

Asks (action items for the week)
- Laura: please sign off on proposed Dedicated burst credit (proposal attached slide 6). Need approval by Thu EOD to configure policy.
- Karthik: confirm if a dynamic fallback routing (latency-first -> cost-first during bursts) can be implemented as a routing policy by Friday so we can show it in the dry run.
- Marcus: please pull the SRE incident log for last week's p4d saturation and attach a one-page root-cause summary.
- Vanessa: align with CS to confirm which Acme workloads can tolerate model-variant fallback; Susan (cc) can provide mapping.

Notes for QBR deck
- Slide 4: show MRR motion + cohort breakout (see prefix_metrics.csv).
- Slide 6: approval ask (burst credit) + cost/revenue modeling.
- Slide 9: escalation playbook (fallback routing + communications cadence).

Attachments:
- [attachment: QBR-deck-v2.pdf (pdf, 2.3MB)]
- [attachment: prefix_metrics.csv (csv, 120KB)]

Thanks — short replies ok if you just have the approvals or a single clarifying question. I’ll compile responses into the QBR notes by Thu 18:00 PT.

—
Jasmine Liu
Sr. PM, Commercial GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Exec Staff <exec-staff@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Park <susan@acme-data.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly Exec Staff Snapshot: Traction, Chokepoints & QBR asks

Jasmine — thanks for the crisp summary. I approve the burst credit proposal in principle for 90 days, contingent on Marcus' RCA and Karthik's routing feasibility.

Two quick clarifications:
- Can you quantify the expected incremental cost (net of projected extra MRR) for the 90-day window? If it’s small relative to the expansion, we should greenlight.
- If we route non-critical traffic to a cheaper variant, do we have a simple SLA communication template for customers affected?

Laura
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Jasmine. Quick notes from infra side:
- Routing policy: we can implement a latency->cost fallback as a policy flag on the router, but it will take ~36 hours to validate and 48 hours more for safe canary in Dedicated. We can show a mock in the QBR; full rollout would be post-QBR.
- Cost estimate for 90-day burst credit: finance-sim indicates a ~0.9% hit to ARR if usage remains at current spike levels; with Acme onboarded, expected incremental ARR covers ~1.7x that cost (early estimate). Detailed numbers attached in the drive link.

Question for Laura / Marcus: what is the acceptable rollback window for the canary? Karthik suggests 2 hours targets for rollback detection.
